input.reasoning_summary:
The initial verdict of CONTRADICTED is maintained after reviewing the challenge evidence.

H1 (Did operating expenses decrease or remain flat?) is REFUTED: E12 explicitly shows total operating expenses increased from $148,531 million in Q2 2025 to $173,145 million in Q2 2026, a rise of $24,614 million (16.6%). This directly contradicts the claim's assertion of no offsetting rise in operating costs.

H2 (Did operating margin improve?) is SUPPORTED: While the counter_numeric computation shows operating margin improved from 11.4% to 13.7%, this does not support the claim. An improving margin percentage means costs grew slower than revenue, but it does NOT mean there was "no offsetting rise in operating costs" - it confirms costs did rise, just at a slower rate than revenue.

H3 (Were there one-time cost reductions?) is SUPPORTED: E19 shows Amazon received approximately $640 million in tariff refunds in Q2 2026, recorded as a reduction to cost of sales. However, this one-time benefit of $640 million is far smaller than the $24.6 billion increase in total operating expenses shown in E12, so it does not materially change the conclusion.

The claim has two components: (1) improving profitability - SUPPORTED by E3; (2) without an offsetting rise in operating costs - CONTRADICTED by E12, E1, E2, and E5. The evidence clearly shows operating expenses rose substantially in Q2 2026, contradicting the second component of the claim.
